==Ingredients==
* [[Cookbook:Eggplant|Eggplant]]
* [[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
==Equipment==
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Pan]]
* [[Cookbook:Fork|Fork]]
* [[Cookbook:Chef's Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Chopping board]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Bowl]]

==Procedure==
# Rub the eggplant with vegetable oil, and prick the skin all over with a fork to make steam vents.
# Place eggplant in a pan, and [[Cookbook:Broiling|broil]] or [[Cookbook:Roasting|roast]] in a hot oven until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft. Let cool.
# Cut the eggplant in half lengthwise. Keep the flesh and discard the burnt skin.
# [[Cookbook:Mincing|Mince]] the eggplant flesh with a knife to get a [[Cookbook:Purée|purée]], keeping the seeds whole. Use a stainless steel or wooden chopper.
# Transfer the eggplant to a bowl, and mix in ½–1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] oil per whole eggplant used. Mix in the onion, and season to taste with salt.
# Chill in the fridge until serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is advisable to use a pan with elevated ridges so that eggplant won't be cooking in its own juices.
